claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar-colony microstructure.
The initial alloy exhibits limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Adding 0.1–0.2 at% boron and applying homogenization and controlled cooling will increase room-temperature yield strength relative to the undoped baseline.
Adding 0.1–0.2 at% boron and applying homogenization and controlled cooling will increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the undoped baseline.
Homogenization at 1100–1200 °C for 2–4 hours will produce a uniform boron distribution.
A mild controlled-cooling schedule will preserve the lamellar spacing.
Boron will segregate to internal lamellar boundaries.
Boron segregation will reduce the energy of internal lamellar boundaries.
Reduced boundary energy from boron segregation will mitigate microcrack initiation at lamellar boundaries.
Boron segregation will strengthen interfaces and enhance interfacial cohesion.
Enhanced interfacial cohesion will reduce early crack propagation and thereby improve ductility.
Boron will provide slight solid-solution strengthening that raises yield strength.
The intervention will increase room-temperature yield strength by approximately 10–20%.
The intervention will increase elongation before fracture by approximately 5–15 percentage points.
The undoped lamellar baseline readily develops microcracks during room-temperature tension.
Boron contents above 0.2 at% may produce additional phases or excessive segregation that causes embrittlement.
Boron additions below 0.1 at% may not significantly improve mechanical properties.
Boundary-doping strategies have previously been effective in other alloy systems.
